ex.en: He felt wretched for days after the argument with his closest friend.
ex.zh: 和最好的朋友吵架后，他难受了好几天。

words.note: wretched 由 wretch 加 -ed 构成，语气强，多指非常难受或恶劣。

ex.en: It seems absurd to buy a new car just because the old one is dirty.
ex.zh: 仅因为旧车脏了就买新车，这似乎很荒唐。

words.note: absurd 比 silly 更正式，语气更强；名词为 absurdity。

ex.en: She accepted the prize with modesty and thanked her whole team.
ex.zh: 她谦虚地领了奖，并感谢了整个团队。

words.note: modesty 是 modest 的名词；反义为 arrogance。

ex.en: It was considerate of you to call and tell us you would be late.
ex.zh: 你打电话告诉我们你会迟到，真是体贴。

words.note: considerate 表体贴的；considerable 表相当大的，注意区分。

ex.en: The film captures the glamor of the city in the nineteen twenties.
ex.zh: 影片捕捉到二十年代这座城市的魅力。

words.note: 美式拼作 glamor，英式 glamour；形容词是 glamorous。

ex.en: The police found a clue to the missing car near the old bridge.
ex.zh: 警方在旧桥附近找到了失踪汽车的线索。

words.note: a clue to sth 用 to 不用 of；have no clue 是口语说法。

ex.en: Put the explanation in brackets so the main sentence stays clear.
ex.zh: 把解释放在括号里，这样主句依然清晰。

words.note: bracket 指方括号或圆括号；年龄、收入档次也用 bracket。

ex.en: The tenants decided to take legal action over the repeated rent increases.
ex.zh: 租户们决定就多次涨租提起诉讼。

words.note: legal 表合法或与法律有关；lawful 多指符合法律，较正式。

ex.en: The company expanded rapidly in the midst of a serious economic downturn.
ex.zh: 公司在经济严重低迷期间迅速扩张。

words.note: midst 只用于 in the midst of 等固定短语，不单独使用。

ex.en: Patience is a personality trait that can be developed with practice.
ex.zh: 耐心是一种性格特征，可以通过练习培养。

words.note: trait 指人的性格或遗传特征；feature 泛指事物特点。

ex.en: Most residents live within a radius of five kilometres from the hospital.
ex.zh: 多数居民住在距医院五公里的半径范围内。

words.note: radius 复数为 radii；within a radius of 是常见搭配。

ex.en: The disintegration of the old empire led to decades of local conflict.
ex.zh: 旧帝国的瓦解导致了数十年的地方冲突。

words.note: dis- 表「分开」，integr 表「整体」；动词为 disintegrate。

ex.en: The phone signal was too weak to send any message from the valley.
ex.zh: 山谷里手机信号太弱，发不出任何消息。

words.note: signal 作动词表示意或标志；作形容词表显著的。

ex.en: Long exposure to loud noise can permanently impair your hearing.
ex.zh: 长期暴露在噪音中会永久损害听力。

words.note: impair 多指功能受损；名词 impairment 比 damage 正式。

ex.en: A school of dolphins followed the boat for more than a mile.
ex.zh: 一群海豚跟着船游了一英里多。

words.note: dolphin 群体用 a school of；它是哺乳动物，不是鱼。

ex.en: We spent the morning sightseeing in the old town before the rain came.
ex.zh: 下雨前我们在老城区观光了一个上午。

words.note: sightseeing 不可数；固定说法 go sightseeing，不加冠词。

ex.en: A stray dog followed the children home from the market.
ex.zh: 一只流浪狗跟着孩子们从市场回了家。

words.note: stray from the point 表离题；stray dog 指走失的狗。

ex.en: Scientists search the sky for planets that might support life.
ex.zh: 科学家在天空中寻找可能支持生命的行星。

words.note: planet 指行星，star 指恒星；地球作天体名常写作 Earth。

ex.en: The long climb exhausted everyone in the group except the guide.
ex.zh: 长途攀登让除向导外的所有人都筋疲力尽。

words.note: be exhausted 表筋疲力尽；作名词 exhaust 指排出的废气。

ex.en: The company moved to Shanghai in 2010 and grew quickly thereafter.
ex.zh: 公司于2010年迁至上海，此后迅速发展。

words.note: thereafter 相当于 after that，正式书面语，口语少用。

ex.en: This powder is fully soluble in cold water, so it mixes quickly.
ex.zh: 这种粉末可完全溶于冷水，因此很容易混合。

words.note: soluble 反义为 insoluble；solute 指溶质。

ex.en: The whole village gathered for a feast at the end of the harvest.
ex.zh: 秋收结束时全村聚在一起享用盛宴。

words.note: feast on sth 表尽情吃；a feast for the eyes 指视觉盛宴。

ex.en: The director has a clear vision of what the museum should become.
ex.zh: 馆长对博物馆的未来有清晰的愿景。

words.note: vision 既指视力也指眼光、愿景；形容词为 visual。

ex.en: Two teachers will accompany the students on the trip to the museum.
ex.zh: 两位老师将陪学生一起参观博物馆。

words.note: accompany 是及物动词，不加 with；被动用 by 引出。

ex.en: The museum displays a complete suit of armor from the fifteenth century.
ex.zh: 博物馆展出一套十五世纪的完整盔甲。

words.note: 美式拼作 armor，英式 armour；a suit of armor 是固定说法。

ex.en: She received an acceptance letter from the university she had hoped for.
ex.zh: 她收到了心仪大学的录取通知书。

words.note: acceptance 是 accept 的名词；gain acceptance 表认可。

ex.en: Moderate exercise is beneficial to both physical and mental health.
ex.zh: 适度运动对身心健康都有益。

words.note: be beneficial to 后接对象；benefit 可作名词或动词。

ex.en: The island has become a tropical paradise for divers and birdwatchers.
ex.zh: 这座岛已成为潜水者和观鸟者的热带天堂。

words.note: paradise 指天堂或乐园；常与 tropical、shoppers 等搭配。

ex.en: The city has finally begun to tackle the problem of air pollution.
ex.zh: 该市终于开始着手处理空气污染问题。

words.note: tackle 常接 problem、issue 等；也可表与某人交涉。

ex.en: I reckon it will take about three hours to finish the report.
ex.zh: 我估计完成这份报告大约要三个小时。

words.note: reckon 口语表认为、估计；reckon on 表指望。
